audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart is a blanket 'Skill' while content and packet both give Mel everything except Level 6 (Galio).
audit.why: Kit supports the shape: Mel out-ranges an immobile tank in the 1v1; Galio's real spike is the global Hero's Entrance at 6 (180s CD). The 45.45% WR reflects his roam/teamfight value, not the lane rows.
audit.corrected: Full phases[0..6].side aligned to content win[] with grounded whys/ratings as one atomic group.

audit.why: Spikes correctly frame 3-5 as Mel's poke-and-pin window, 6 as Galio's global spike, first item as continued Mel range edge, and late as his teamfight taunt. All 4 present.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both flagged missing interactions absent (Colossal Smash auto-reset tell; Justice Punch cutting retreat with no Mel dash — hold Flash for the wall); no digits in cooldowns; two bleed bullets.
audit.why: P is an auto-reset AoE — its wind-up is the step-back cue. E Justice Punch (11s, 650 range) telegraphs with a step-back before charging and is Galio's only engage. Q Winds of War (11s) is a projectile Rebuttal returns. W Shield of Durand 18s.
audit.corrected: Auto-reset tell into dontsFull[0].d; Flash-for-the-wall into tradeBad; snare-the-wind-up into dosFull[1].d; numbers into breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by shoving with Winds of War, vanishing on a global Hero's Entrance, and cashing kills in the other lanes.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Eating Justice Punch with Flash down — the punch cuts off retreat and you have no dash, so hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.

edits.after: Q-volley his last-hits — Galio has no answer at 950 range while his W shield sits on cooldown.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Late his value is the global and the taunt, not the duel — out-poke him and track Hero's Entrance.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1 — his only engage; he has none while it's down. - Shield of Durand is 18s: poke while it recharges. - Hero's Entrance is 180s: a spent global buys minutes of safe sidelanes. - Never spend Rebuttal on poke.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Justice Punch telegraphs — he steps back before the charge; drop Solar Snare on the wind-up and the knockup never arrives.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Colossal Smash's auto-reset winds up first — up close the tell comes too late.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: A loaded Justice Punch reaches 650 — volley from beyond it or keep moving; a stationary Mel is the exact target the dash was made for.

notes: Packet defect (chart Mel 6/7 vs 45.45% WR) noted: the chart shape is kit-grounded (Galio's win rate comes from roam/teamfight value, not lane rows), so I aligned the full layer to the content/packet chart rather than flipping rows. Whether Solar Snare's root actually cancels a mid-flight Justice Punch is unverified — I phrased it as snaring the step-back wind-up, which Riot's text supports; content wants.you[2] ('interrupt E with E') left as-is, unverified.
